author: ch402
text: @yonashav @nathanbenaich The motivating moment for me was that I went on a walk with a senior colleague shortly before I left Google Brain, and they matter of factly told me that "all interpretability is bullshit" because they'd been so turned off by saliency maps.

author: ch402
text:
@nathanbenaich I was motivated by many of my colleagues at Google Brain being deeply skeptical of things like saliency maps.

When I started the OpenAI interpretability team, I used it to distinguish our goal: understand how the weights of a neural network map to algorithms.

author: ch402
text: @nathanbenaich I introduced the term to distinguish the work I was doing on circuits from a lot of other work that was going on circa 2018, notably saliency maps.

author: ch402
text: What a remarkable job of balancing accessibility and technical accuracy! If you're familiar with the content, it's very fun to watch. If you're not familiar, it's a very nice way to dip a toe in.

quoted.text: In our new video, we talk about research on interpreting InceptionV1, a convolutional neural network. Researchers have been able to understand the function of neurons and channels inside the network and uncover visual processing algorithms by looking at the weights. author: ch402
text: Very exciting to see more work applying SAEs to frontier models! Lots of nice contributions: scaling laws, explorations of new methods that push the (L0,MSE) frontier, new eval approaches...

quoted.text:
Excited to share what I've been working on as part of the former Superalignment team!

We introduce a SOTA training stack for SAEs. To demonstrate that our methods scale, we train a 16M latent SAE on GPT-4. Because MSE/L0 is not the final goal, we also introduce new SAE metrics.

author: ch402
text: I'm honestly kind of shocked we're here.
